PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 5, audited at commit 68302d5 (committed; working tree carries only
sprint bookkeeping). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict,
including the 16 Aug re-scope that gives up preview database isolation.

VERDICT: PASS.

R2 is the criterion this sprint said mattered most, and it is the first thing in this
project I have been able to verify by mutation rather than by reading. I exported the
tree at 68302d5 to a scratch copy and edited the REAL workflow file three ways:

  widened   if: github.event_name == 'push'                  -> test FAILED (exit 1)
  removed   (no `if` on the migrate job at all)               -> test FAILED (exit 1)
  redirected refs/heads/main -> refs/heads/anything           -> test FAILED (exit 1)
  baseline  unmodified                                        -> test passed

That is R2's requirement met in the form it asked for: "verified by a check that
fails if the workflow's branch condition is removed or widened, not by reading the
condition and believing it." lib/ci-guardrails.test.ts reads the actual
.github/workflows/ci.yml off disk, parses it, and compares jobs.migrate.if to a
pinned constant. It runs in the default `npm run test`, which the build job runs,
which migrate declares in `needs` -- so widening the gate fails the build, which
skips migrate, which means the widened gate never gets to apply anything. The
enforcement chain closes properly.

Requirements coverage:
R1 MET. README's "Shared database (deliberate, Sprint 5)" section states the
  decision, the reasoning (public test data, no accounts, nothing with a privacy
  surface), what isolation would have cost, the consequences spelled out as
  consequences, and an explicit "This changes if:" naming real user data, more than
  one practitioner, or any privacy surface. The acceptance criterion demanded a
  later reader be able to tell this was decided rather than overlooked. They can.
R2 MET. See the mutation results above.
R3 MET. The ordering is structural, not incidental: vercel.json sets
  git.deploymentEnabled.main = false, removing Vercel's independent git-triggered
  production deploy, and the only remaining trigger is the last step of the migrate
  job -- which is reached only after build and rls-tests pass, the migration applies,
  and the drift check comes back clean. The deployment is gated on migration
  success rather than running alongside it, which is the criterion verbatim. See
  note 2 for the part of the race this narrows rather than closes.
R4 MET. README's "Migrations: expand, then contract" is written as a standing rule
  for every future migration, not a description of this one, and it gives concrete
  operational rules (nullable or defaulted before required; add before write; do not
  drop until no deployed version reads it; never combine add-new and remove-old in
  one migration) plus the reason -- rollback moves the application, not the database.
  That last sentence is what makes the rule stick.
R5 NOT STATICALLY VERIFIABLE, and correctly so. An executed rollback is
  GroundTruth's third criterion and the sprint file is right that a procedure nobody
  has run is a hypothesis. Nothing I can do from a diff changes that. What I can
  confirm is that the observable exists: the homepage still renders
  VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA, unchanged since Sprint 1, so the rollback has something to
  be measured against.
R6 MET, all four items. docs/RUNBOOK.md covers rolling back an app deploy (with the
  Instant Rollback mechanics and the cross-check against the SHA the page displayed);
  a migration needing undoing as a forward-fix with no reverse-migration mechanism,
  and why; an explicit "Deciding which procedure an incident needs" section splitting
  code-broken from schema-wrong from both, using /api/health/db's version and the
  homepage SHA as the two observables; and the shared-database exception with the
  two preview symptoms that are expected behaviour rather than incidents. The
  cross-reference between the rollback procedure and expand-then-contract -- an app
  rollback is only safe if the old code's schema still exists -- is the part most
  runbooks omit and the part that actually matters at 3am.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 11 tests across 4 files.
- next build exits 0; route table unchanged.
- Rebuilt with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="QA1PROBESERVICEROLE" and grepped all of
  .next: absent from the entire build output.
- vercel.json parses as valid JSON with the documented shape.
- The README's claim that a missing deploy-hook secret fails loudly rather than
  silently not deploying: `curl -fsS -X POST ""` exits 2. Accurate.

Notes, not conditions:
1. The guardrail does not cover two other ways the same protection can be undone. I
   probed both against the real file rather than assuming:
     - dropping rls-tests from migrate's `needs` (back to `needs: build`)
       -> guardrail PASSES. That silently undoes the condition I required in
       Sprint 4 round 2.
     - moving the "Trigger production deployment" step out of migrate into its own
       ungated job -> guardrail PASSES, and every push on every branch would then
       deploy to production.
   Both are met criteria-wise: R2 scopes the check to the migration job's branch
   condition, and that is exactly what it delivers. I am not holding the sprint for
   coverage Master Controller did not ask for. But this sprint's whole argument is
   that a condition someone reads and trusts is not enforcement, and the deploy
   trigger it just created -- now the sole path to production -- is sitting outside
   the check it sits next to. Extending ci-guardrails.test.ts to assert migrate's
   `needs` and that the deploy step lives inside migrate is about six lines against
   machinery that already exists. Worth doing before the next person edits this file.
2. A Vercel Deploy Hook builds the branch's latest commit at the moment it fires, not
   the commit whose CI run fired it. So the race is narrowed rather than closed: a
   deploy can no longer start without a successful migrate run (that was the Sprint 2
   race, and it is genuinely fixed), but if a second push lands on main while the
   first push's migrate job is still running, the first hook deploys the newer tip,
   whose own migration has not been applied yet. Its own CI run will apply it moments
   later. Under R4's expand-then-contract rule that window is survivable by design,
   which is the correct answer -- worth stating so the residual window is known
   rather than assumed away.
3. HANDOFF ITEM, and the most important one here. The sprint file's Dependencies say
   "External: None." That is no longer true: this sprint introduces
   secrets.VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL, which requires creating a Deploy Hook in the
   Vercel dashboard targeting main and adding its URL as a GitHub Actions secret.
   README documents the procedure well, so this is a sprint-file gap rather than a
   code defect. But the consequence is sharp: main's automatic git deploy is now off,
   so until that secret exists, production does not deploy at all. The failure is
   loud (curl exits 2, migrate fails) and, importantly, it fails AFTER the migration
   has already applied -- schema advances, code does not. That is exactly the state
   R4's expand-then-contract rule makes safe, so the design is coherent under its own
   failure mode, which I do not often get to write down. Set the secret before
   Pipeman ships, not after.
4. vercel.json's git.deploymentEnabled disables main only, so preview branches should
   still deploy as before. I cannot verify Vercel's behaviour from a diff, and this
   sprint's R1 depends on it entirely. GroundTruth's first criterion -- a preview
   deployment loads and serves the application -- is the check that settles it, and
   it should be run against a real preview branch rather than inferred.
5. Carried forward from Sprint 4, both still open and both in the file this sprint
   touched: the "Export local stack URL/anon key" step is now a pipe under a shell
   with -e but not pipefail, so a failing `supabase status` no longer fails that step
   (add `shell: bash`); and `supabase status -o env` dumps every status variable
   including the local stack's SERVICE_ROLE_KEY into the job environment when only
   the two NEXT_PUBLIC_ ones are needed (pipe through `grep -E '^NEXT_PUBLIC_'`).
   Neither is dangerous today. Both are three-line edits in a file this sprint was
   already editing, which is the cheapest they will ever be.

Sprint 5 shipped no migration -- git diff --stat 3648d7a..68302d5 touches ci.yml, README.md, docs/RUNBOOK.md, lib/ci-guardrails.ts and its test, package.json, package-lock.json, vercel.json, and nothing under supabase/migrations/. All three migrations are identical at both commits. WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, recorded so nobody reads more into this PASS than it earned: because Sprint 5 shipped no schema change, the app was rolled back to the exact version its schema was built for. App and schema stayed matched throughout. This verifies that a rollback returns the application to its prior version. It does NOT exercise R4's expand-then-contract rule, and it is not evidence that a schema tolerates being rolled back under. The first real test of that will be the first rollback across a migration boundary, which has not happened yet. CRITERION 1 -- a preview deployment loads and serves the application. NOT TESTED. vercel ls --environment preview -> "No deployments found under bent-metal." git ls-remote --heads origin -> refs/heads/main, and nothing else. There is no preview deployment on this project and never has been; all six deployments in the project's history are target: production. The branch push that would create one had not landed as of 16:47:28Z. CRITERION 2 -- production continues to serve correctly WITH THE PREVIEW IN EXISTENCE. NOT TESTED, and I am declining to close it on the evidence available. I was asked to close this one in the same pass on the grounds that production plainly serves correctly by anonymous fetch. Production does serve correctly -- that is fully evidenced under criterion 3 above, and I am not disputing the observation. But the criterion is not "production serves correctly". It is production continuing to serve correctly *with a preview in existence*. The whole content of the criterion is the coexistence: that standing up a preview environment, which R1 says shares the production Supabase database, does not disturb production. With zero previews in existence, there is nothing for production to be coexisting with, and a green result here would be evidence about a condition that was never created. Recording it as passed would put a claim in the sprint record that no observation supports. This is a ten-second re-check once a preview exists, and I will run it the moment one does. BLOCKER FOR CRITERION 1, already established this session and unresolved. Vercel SSO deployment protection is active on non-alias deployment URLs: GET https://my-little-racoon-jw2mw95kg-bent-metal.vercel.app/ -> 302, location: https://vercel.com/sso-api?url=...&nonce=... -> /login Preview deployments inherit this by default. So creating the preview branch is necessary but not sufficient: an anonymous fetch of the resulting preview URL will return a Vercel login page, not the application, and I will not be able to verify that it "loads and serves the application". This needs a protection bypass token, previews set to public, or an authenticated browser session, and this session has no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension. Resolve it before the preview is created, not after. OPERATIONAL NOTE, NOT PART OF ANY CRITERION -- IMPORTANT. Production is running Sprint 4's code (3648d7a) as of this verdict. It must be promoted back to 68302d5 (Vercel deployment jw2mw95kg) before Sprint 6 starts. That is a Pipeman action and it is outstanding right now. I have recorded this verdict against the rolled-back state deliberately, because that state was the observation window for criterion 3; it is not a statement that production should stay there. If the promote is skipped, every later live test will be run against the wrong code and Sprint 5's own shipped changes will not be in production. TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. Checks are curl over HTTPS against production plus the authenticated Vercel CLI for deployment enumeration. The page is statically prerendered so the SHA check is sound. No browser rendering was observed and I am not claiming any.

FAIL: GroundTruth live test round 2, Sprint 5, commit
68302d5dcb374dd1512560edd6e337377ea7a104.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the Bent Metal Vercel
project, 2026-08-16 16:52-16:58Z.

VERDICT: FAIL. The enabling action was performed and the expected result did not
occur. Pushing a branch does NOT create a preview deployment in this project's
current configuration, so criterion 1 is not merely untested -- it is
unachievable by the prescribed method, and criterion 2 depends on it.

Criterion 3 passed in round 1 and is not re-litigated here.

WHAT WAS DONE, AND WHAT DID NOT HAPPEN
  - Branch pushed: refs/heads/preview-check now exists on origin at
    68302d5dcb374dd1512560edd6e337377ea7a104. Confirmed via git ls-remote --heads.
  - CI fired on that branch: run 31959914230, triggered 16:52:55Z, completed
    successfully -- build 34s, rls-tests 1m56s.
  - Preview deployment created: NONE. `vercel ls --environment preview` returned
    "No deployments found under bent-metal." on eight separate polls between
    16:55:15Z and 16:58:16Z, roughly five and a half minutes after the push.
  - This is not a build still in flight. Every production deployment in this
    project's history completed in 15-29 seconds. Five minutes is an order of
    magnitude past that.
  - `vercel ls` unfiltered still shows exactly six deployments, all
    target: production, the newest being jw2mw95kg from 40 minutes ago. Nothing
    new was created by the branch push at all.

CRITERION 1 -- a preview deployment loads and serves the application. FAIL.
  There is no preview deployment to load. No preview deployment has ever existed
  on this project.

CRITERION 2 -- production continues to serve correctly with the preview in
existence. NOT TESTED, blocked by criterion 1. Unchanged from round 1: the
criterion's content is the coexistence, and there is still nothing for production
to coexist with. Production itself is healthy and correctly restored -- see below
-- but that is not this criterion.

WHY, AS FAR AS I CAN OBSERVE FROM OUTSIDE. Stated as evidence first, then
hypothesis clearly marked as such.

  Evidence:
  - vercel.json at the deployed commit contains, in full:
      {"git":{"deploymentEnabled":{"main":false}}}
    This disables Vercel's automatic git deploy for `main` only. It says nothing
    about other branches, so on its own it should not prevent a preview from
    `preview-check`.
  - Production deployments are triggered exclusively by a deploy hook:
    ci.yml's `Trigger production deployment` step runs
    `curl -fsS -X POST "${{ secrets.VERCEL_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL }}"`, and it lives
    inside the `migrate` job, which is gated
    `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'`.
  - On the preview-check run, `migrate` shows as skipped (0s). So no deploy hook
    fired for this branch, by design. Nothing in CI creates a preview.
  - `vercel project inspect my-little-racoon` returns General, Framework Settings
    and nothing else. No connected Git repository is listed in its output.

  Hypothesis, NOT confirmed: the project has no Vercel Git integration connected
  (it was linked with the CLI -- .vercel/project.json exists), so no push to any
  branch produces an automatic deployment of any kind. I cannot confirm this from
  outside; `vercel project inspect` not printing a git section is suggestive, not
  proof, and I have no dashboard access. Note that this would be a CHANGE from
  earlier in this project's life: in Sprints 1 and 2 pushes to main did produce
  deployments without any deploy hook, which is why Sprint 1's README documents
  that CI did not gate the Vercel deploy. Whoever picks this up should check the
  project's Git settings in the dashboard first, before changing any code.

  A SECOND, RELATED THING WORTH CHECKING, and I am flagging it precisely because I
  cannot settle it from here. ci.yml's comment above the deploy step says
  vercel.json's git.deploymentEnabled.main = false is what makes the deploy hook
  "the only path a production deployment can start from", and calls it the fix for
  the race named in Sprint 2. If the Git integration is in fact not connected,
  then that setting is currently inert -- Vercel was not going to auto-deploy from
  a push regardless -- and the race is closed by the absence of the integration
  rather than by the config. The config would still be correct and load-bearing
  the moment anyone reconnects the repo, so this is not an argument for removing
  it. It is an argument for knowing which of the two mechanisms is actually
  holding, because if it is the accidental one, reconnecting Git to get previews
  working could quietly reintroduce the Sprint 2 race unless deploymentEnabled is
  verified at the same time. Fixing criterion 1 and preserving R3 are the same
  piece of work, and doing one without checking the other is how the race comes
  back.

POSITIVE FINDING, VERIFIED LIVE -- R2's main-only migration restriction holds.
  This is the criterion the sprint file calls "the criterion that matters most in
  this sprint", and while it is QA1's to audit statically, the branch push
  produced live evidence for it: on run 31959914230 from refs/heads/preview-check,
  `migrate` was skipped outright (0s, never started), while build and rls-tests
  both ran and passed. An unreviewed branch did not touch the production schema.
  Recording it because it was observed, not because it was asked for.

PRODUCTION STATE, CONFIRMED HEALTHY AND CORRECTLY RESTORED
  The promote back from the rollback was performed. Production alias now serves
  title="68302d5dcb374dd1512560edd6e337377ea7a104", i.e. Sprint 5's code, not
  Sprint 4's. The outstanding item I flagged in round 1 is closed. Production is
  in the right state for Sprint 6 to start on.

WHAT WOULD CLEAR THIS
  1. Determine why a branch push produces no preview deployment -- check the
     Vercel project's Git integration and its preview settings in the dashboard
     first, since no code change is warranted until that is known.
  2. If reconnecting or re-enabling Git integration is the fix, verify at the same
     time that vercel.json's git.deploymentEnabled.main = false is actually in
     effect, so R3's ordering guarantee survives the change.
  3. Resolve the Vercel SSO deployment protection blocker from round 1, still
     unaddressed: non-alias deployment URLs return
     302 -> https://vercel.com/sso-api?url=...&nonce=... -> /login. Previews
     inherit this by default, so even once a preview exists, an anonymous fetch
     will retrieve a Vercel login page rather than the application. Needs a
     protection bypass token, previews set to public, or an authenticated browser
     session; this session has neither Playwright MCP nor the Chrome extension.
  Then reship and I re-test criteria 1 and 2.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. Checks are
curl over HTTPS against production, the authenticated Vercel CLI for deployment
and project enumeration, and the gh CLI for CI state. No browser rendering was
observed and I am not claiming any.
